fixtures.basis: Virginia's Uniform Statewide Building Code supersedes the building codes and regulations of cities (Code of Virginia § 36-98, quoted in the state pack from law.lis.virginia.gov), so Norfolk cannot amend the toilet-count table or its rules. Nothing on Norfolk's permit pages changes the counts. The state pack's worked examples stand.

permit.exempt_list_quote: B. Section 108.2 Exemptions from application for permit. Notwithstanding the requirements of Section 108.1, application for a permit and any related inspections shall not be required for the following; however, this section shall not be construed to exempt such activities from other applicable requirements of this code. [...] 13. Construction work deemed by the building official to be minor and ordinary and that does not adversely affect public health or general safety. 14. Ordinary repairs that include the following: [...] 14.2. Replacement of plumbing fixtures and well pumps in all groups without alteration of the water supply and distribution systems, sanitary drainage systems, or vent systems. [...] 14.7. Installation or replacement of floor finishes in all occupancies. 14.8. Replacement of Class C interior wall or ceiling finishes installed in Groups A, E, and I and replacement of all classes of interior wall or ceiling finishes in other groups. 14.9. Installation or replacement of cabinetry or trim. 14.10. Application of paint or wallpaper. 14.11. Other repair work deemed by the building official to be minor and ordinary which does not adversely affect public health or general safety.
permit.required_quote: A. Section 108.1 When applications are required. Application for a permit shall be made to the building official and a permit shall be obtained prior to the commencement of any of the following activities [...] 1. Construction or demolition of a building or structure. Installations or alterations involving (i) the removal or addition of any wall, partition, or portion thereof; (ii) any structural component; (iii) the repair or replacement of any required component of a fire or smoke rated assembly; (iv) the alteration of any required means of egress system, including the addition or removal of emergency supplemental hardware; (v) water supply and distribution system, sanitary drainage system, or vent system; (vi) electric wiring; (vii) fire protection system, mechanical systems, or fuel supply systems; or (viii) any equipment regulated by the USBC.
permit.city_quote: When do I need a Building Permit? A building permit is required for any residential or commercial repair (alteration), addition, or new construction that requires new framing or exposes existing framing. [...] Commercial projects: building permits are required to remove drywall, construct new partition walls or bearing walls, relocate walls, install new framing, re-roof, side or cover exterior walls, complete tenant build-outs, complete change in use, obtain a change in occupancy, build additions, construct commercial accessory structures, install fences taller than 6 feet in height, install fire suppression equipment, install 5 foot run-ins, elevators, install paint booths, construct service station islands and canopies, and install pre-manufactured steel buildings. When is a permit not required? Building permits are not required for 1 and 2 family residential re-roofs, replacement windows of the same size, vinyl or shake siding, cabinets, floor coverings, minor repair to decks including but not limited to deck board repair and tread repair, driveways, water tanks supported on grade at 5,000 gallons or less, retaining walls supporting less than 2 feet of unbalanced fill, and above ground swimming pools less than 2 feet deep.
permit.note: The exempt list is the state's (13VAC5-63-80, Section 108.2 of the Virginia Construction Code), which applies in Norfolk; Norfolk's own page gives a shorter plain-language list. Neither names toilet partitions or toilet compartments. Section 108.1 requires a permit for work 'involving the removal or addition of any wall, partition, or portion thereof'; it does not say whether a toilet stall partition is a 'partition' in that sense, and the question is not decided here. Whether the building official treats a like-for-like replacement as 'minor and ordinary' (items 13 and 14.11) is his decision.
permit.office: City of Norfolk Development Services Center (Department of City Planning, Building Safety Division), 810 Union Street, 1st Floor
permit.phone_quote: Who can I contact if I have questions? Please call 757-664-6565 for assistance. Questions can also be sent to planreviewpermits@norfolk.gov.

restrooms_city.note: No Norfolk ordinance on single-user restroom signs or shared all-gender rooms was found: one web search returned nothing for Norfolk, and Norfolk's permit pages say nothing about restrooms. The Norfolk City Code itself (Municode) could not be read, so this is 'none found', not 'none exists'. Because the statewide building code supersedes local building regulations, the state rules in the state pack (single-user rooms marked for everyone; multi-user all-gender rooms allowed with floor-to-ceiling compartments) apply in Norfolk as written.

public_wage.state_law_note: Virginia has a prevailing wage law (§ 2.2-4321.3): mandatory for state agencies on public works over $250,000, and for a locality only if it adopts an ordinance. The Department of Labor and Industry publishes no rate table; its page says determinations 'are based on the applicable prevailing wage rate determinations made by the U.S. Secretary of Labor under the provisions of the Davis-Bacon Act', and the statute says the state rate may 'in no event' be lower than the Davis-Bacon rate. So the federal determination for Norfolk is the published figure, and the floor for a state determination.
public_wage.state_law_quote: "Prevailing wage rate" means the rate [...] as determined by the Commissioner on the basis of surveys conducted every three years, provided that (i) in no event shall the prevailing wage rate be lower than the prevailing wage rate determined by the U.S. Secretary of Labor under the provisions of the federal Davis-Bacon Act [...] C. Notwithstanding any other provision of this chapter, any locality may adopt an ordinance requiring that, when letting contracts for public works paid for in whole or in part by funds of the locality [...] N. The provisions of this section shall not apply to any public contract for public works of $250,000 or less.
public_wage.city_rule_note: Norfolk prevailing wage ordinance under § 2.2-4321.3 C: none found. Three web searches (ordinance, council vote, city code wage rules) returned no Norfolk ordinance, agenda item or news report, while the same searches returned Richmond's (in effect July 1, 2025), Arlington's, Fairfax's and Prince William's. Norfolk's Purchasing page and its Contracts page (the December 2020 inclusive procurement ordinance, with minority-owned and women-owned business spending goals) mention no wage requirement. Chapter 33.1 of the Norfolk City Code (procurement) could not be read: Municode blocks automated access. This is 'none found', not 'confirmed none'. No city living wage rule on contracts was found on the way either.

page.meta: Commercial bathroom partitions delivered to Norfolk job sites. Price your restroom, pick a material and see the Virginia rules Norfolk enforces.
page.lead: Commercial bathroom partitions for Norfolk offices, port and shipyard buildings, university halls and medical centers, shipped by freight to your job site.
page.stall_bullet: - **How many stalls:** Virginia's statewide rules set the number of toilets by how many people use the building. A city can't change them, so Norfolk enforces them as the state writes them. The table below shows what that means.
page.permit_bullet: - **Permits:** the City of Norfolk's Development Services Center issues building permits. Virginia's statewide rules require a permit for work that adds or removes a wall or partition or changes the plumbing. They exempt replacing plumbing fixtures without touching the pipes, installing or replacing cabinetry or trim, and work the building official considers minor and ordinary. Neither list names toilet partitions, and Norfolk's own permit page doesn't either, so ask the Development Services Center (757-664-6565) whether your replacement needs one. You don't need a permit to buy partitions.
page.confirm_office: the City of Norfolk's Development Services Center
page.install_rule: Contractors working in Norfolk need a city business license, which requires workers' compensation coverage where the state requires it. Virginia requires a state contractor license for commercial jobs over $1,000: Class C covers single jobs up to $30,000, Class B up to $150,000, and Class A $150,000 and above. Norfolk's building permit application asks for the contractor's Virginia license number and class. Confirm with the Norfolk Commissioner of the Revenue and the Virginia Board for Contractors. You don't need a permit to buy partitions.
page.faq_install_extra: On a job over $1,000, the contractor needs a Virginia contractor license, and a Norfolk business license to work in the city.
page.public_jobs_bullet: - **Public jobs:** on state agency projects over $250,000, Virginia law requires at least the prevailing wage set by the state's Commissioner of Labor and Industry, and a city, county or school division has to pay it only if it has passed its own ordinance. The state bases its rates on the federal ones and may not set them lower. The federal rate for a carpenter on building work in the City of Norfolk is $19.80 an hour plus $3.98 in benefits. For a City of Norfolk project, ask the city's Purchasing Office whether a wage requirement applies.
page.sales_tax_bullet: - **Sales tax:** 6% in Norfolk: 4.3% state, 1% city and a 0.7% regional tax that applies across Hampton Roads.
page.buyers_extra: - **Port, shipyard and waterfront facilities:** solid plastic or phenolic with stainless steel hardware, for restrooms that see heavy boots, washdown and damp air.
sources: - Codes enforced in Norfolk: the statewide code applies in every Virginia city (see the state sources below); the city enforces it through the Building Safety Division at the Development Services Center, 810 Union Street: City of Norfolk, [Permits and Inspections](https://www.norfolk.gov/2799/Permits-and-Inspections), [Building Permits](https://www.norfolk.gov/6538/Building-Permits) and the [Commercial Building Permit Application packet](https://www.norfolk.gov/DocumentCenter/View/72677/COMMERCIAL-Packet-redo-fillable). Checked 2026-11-24.

- When a permit is needed and what is exempt: [13VAC5-63-80, Virginia Uniform Statewide Building Code, Section 108, Application for permit](https://law.lis.virginia.gov/admincode/title13/agency5/chapter63/section80/) (Section 108.1, work that needs a permit; Section 108.2, exemptions), and the City of Norfolk's [Permits and Inspections](https://www.norfolk.gov/2799/Permits-and-Inspections) page ("When do I need a Building Permit?", "When is a permit not required?", phone 757-664-6565). Neither names toilet partitions. Checked 2026-11-24.

- Sales tax in Norfolk: Virginia Tax, [Sales and Use Tax](https://www.tax.virginia.gov/sales-and-use-tax) (6% in Hampton Roads, Norfolk listed) and its [Sales Tax Rates by Locality](https://www.tax.virginia.gov/sites/default/files/inline-files/sales-and-use-tax-rates-by-locality-by-date.xlsx) spreadsheet (Norfolk 6% since July 1, 2013); the parts are in the Code of Virginia sections listed under Sales tax below. Checked 2026-11-24.

- Carpenter rate on federally funded building work in the City of Norfolk: [federal wage determination VA20260160, modification 2, May 18, 2026](https://sam.gov/wage-determination/VA20260160/2). State rates are based on the federal ones and may not be lower: [Code of Virginia § 2.2-4321.3](https://law.lis.virginia.gov/vacode/title2.2/chapter43/section2.2-4321.3/) and [Virginia Department of Labor and Industry, Prevailing Wage Law](https://doli.virginia.gov/labor-law/prevailing-wage-law/). Checked 2026-11-24.

- Contractor license details on the permit application and license lookup: City of Norfolk, [Residential Building Permit Application packet](https://www.norfolk.gov/DocumentCenter/View/66067) (Virginia license number and class) and [Hiring a Contractor](https://www.norfolk.gov/5088/Hiring-a-Contractor); business license issued by the Commissioner of the Revenue: [Business Licensing](https://www.norfolk.gov/744/Business-Licensing). Checked 2026-11-24.
page.official_names: 2010 ADA Standards for Accessible Design; ICC A117.1-2017 as referenced by the 2021 Virginia Construction Code; 2021 Virginia Uniform Statewide Building Code, Part I, Virginia Construction Code (2021 International Building Code with Virginia amendments, 13VAC5-63), in force since January 18, 2024, enforced in Norfolk by the Building Safety Division of the Department of City Planning without local amendments (Code of Virginia § 36-98); 2021 Virginia Plumbing Code (2021 International Plumbing Code with Virginia amendments); Section 108 of the Virginia Construction Code (13VAC5-63-80) for permits; NFPA 286 for HDPE.
notes: To confirm by phone before launch: whether replacing or adding toilet partitions in an existing commercial restroom needs a Norfolk building permit, and whether the building official reads 'the removal or addition of any wall, partition, or portion thereof' to include toilet stall partitions (Development Services Center, 757-664-6565, planreviewpermits@norfolk.gov).

Norfolk prevailing wage ordinance: none found in three web searches or on the city's Purchasing and Contracts pages; the City Code's procurement chapter (33.1, on Municode) could not be read. The page therefore doesn't say Norfolk has none: it tells the buyer to ask the Purchasing Office. Confirm in a browser or by phone, then say it outright.

The Norfolk City Code (Municode) blocks automated access: no check of the code itself for a restroom sign rule, a wage rule or the buildings chapter. A browser check of the code for 'restroom', 'toilet' and 'prevailing wage' closes all three.
Norfolk's website has no adopted-codes text of its own: its 'Virginia Construction Codes' page redirects to the ICC's list of Virginia codes. The edition and date are the state's (DHCD).
The carpenter rate in the federal determination is a 2016 survey rate (SUVA2013-043) and sits below the metro median wage shown in the bullet above it.
The four building types in the lead and the buyers bullet on port, shipyard and waterfront facilities are editorial, not sourced.

The federal wage determination's class is 'Carpenter, includes acoustical ceiling installation, drywall hanging, and form work'; whether partition installers are classed as carpenters on a given job is the contracting agency's call.
